issues.problem: NEW this round, meaning defect: 'Malinaw'. In Filipino malinaw means clear in the sense of transparent, sharp or legible (clear water, a clear answer, a clear image); it is not a weather word. The key renders in the weather pill as the direct antonym of rain - js/ui.js:83 writes (isRaining ? Ulan : clear) with a sun glyph - so a Filipino player reads 'Rain / Transparent'. All 19 peer locales use a fair-weather word here: es Despejado, pt-BR Limpo, it Sereno, tr Açık, de Klar, fr Clair, id/ms Cerah, ru/uk Ясно, pl Pogodnie, vi Quang. The correct terms are maaraw (cloudless, sunny) or maliwanag (bright, clear skies). Same file, same contrast pair: rainy 'Ulan' is correct, so only this half of the pair is wrong.
issues.fix: Maaraw   (6 chars; 'Maliwanag' if the owner prefers the more general word)

issues.problem: Follow-up on the applied fix, length/house-pattern only. Choosing the full word for the live HUD key makes fil's temp the longest of all 19 locales at 11 chars, against es/de/fr/it/pl/pt-BR 'Temp.'(5), ru/uk 'Темп'(4), id/ms 'Suhu'(4), tr 'Sıcaklık'(8); median is 5. temp is also the only one of the pair that renders - js/ui.js:78 composes 'temp: <value> degC . days: <n>' into #topR .rw. Measured for that composed row: fil ~183px at the desktop fs-xs 12px where en/ru are ~140px and es ~145px; on mobile the same row is ~137px against the hard cap js/mobile.js:32 puts on #topR (max-width:140px at font-size 9px), i.e. ~3px of headroom, so once totalDays reaches 3 digits the row is ~142px and the top-right pill wraps to two lines. dTemp has no render site at all (see the code note), so keeping 'Temperatura' there costs nothing in pixels and the split loses no internal consistency.
issues.fix: temp: 'Temp.' (keep dTemp: 'Temperatura') - this is exactly the es split (temp 'Temp.' / dTemp 'Temperatura') and restores ~30px of mobile headroom. Acceptable to leave as is if the owner accepts the wrap at 3-digit day counts.

Length is not the problem (25 vs es 28); it is a visible DNA-panel label (js/ui_menus.js:176 group).

Verified against the real layout, and there is no fil-specific overflow defect. Only the .short keys print on the bottom action bar (js/main.js:375-378 labelBtn sets min-width 72px, padding 12px 16px, font-size 15px, and .ab is white-space:nowrap, weight 800 per v3-webgl/index.html:46), plus flight and follow on the same bar. Measured text width at 15px bold, plus the 32px of horizontal padding: HATI 68px, KAIN 69px, Lipad 70px, ILAW 70px, AUTO 75px, SPORA 85px, Sundan 85px. So two values do exceed the 72px floor - hud.btn.cyst.short 'SPORA' and follow 'Sundan' - with hud.btn.auto.short 'AUTO' at 74.5px. All three are baseline-equivalent or better: AUTO is byte-identical to the en value it shares (74.5 vs 74.5), SPORA is 5 letters against en SPORE's 5 (85.4 vs 83.7, within the glyph-estimate error, and ru СПОРА is 45px of text), Sundan 6 letters is the same length as es Seguir and shorter than ru Следить (95px). fil is also the locale that shortens the light pair, LIWANAG(7) -> ILAW(4), which puts it UNDER en LIGHT (76.8px) instead of over it. min-width is a floor, not a cap, and nowrap means the button widens rather than clipping; on mobile .is-mobile .ab drops to min-width 44px / font-size 11px (js/mobile.js:22), where SPORA measures ~52px and fits. The 7-letter LIWANAG and the non-short hud.btn.cyst/divide/eat/menu values never compete for that budget because they have zero render sites.
